xfenced.py.summary: Extract the Python fenced code blocks of Markdown files into ``ex01.py``-style files.
details: Reads the ``.md`` files given on the command line (or all of them in the current directory), matches the ```python / ```py fences and writes each block to a numbered script next to them.

xip.py.summary: Print the public IP address and its country and city via ipinfo.
details: Loads the ``IPINFO_TOKEN`` from ``~/.env`` with python-dotenv, queries the ipinfo service and prints the address, the country and the city in colour.
xip.py.notes: Runs at import time and needs ``IPINFO_TOKEN`` in ``~/.env``.

xm.py.summary: Turn the module docstrings of a source tree into prompt files.
details: Extracts the module docstring of every Python file with ast, reformats it into 80-column prose without its ``LiveDoc:`` line and writes one ``.txt`` per module into the prompt directory, optionally also a ``modules.json`` index; ``--remove`` strips the docstring from the source file instead.

xordup.py.summary: Find the duplicate files of the current directory with an xor hash.
details: Hashes every non-empty file in parallel with ``xorhash``, groups the identical hashes and prints each group; ``-r`` keeps the first file of a group and deletes the rest.

xpy_entities.py.summary: Extract the classes, functions, constants and comments of Python sources with an ast/tree-sitter/libcst backend.
details: Subcommands: ``extract`` writes the entities per kind to ``output/`` as Python, JSON, text or SQLite files, ``nodes``/``sexpr``/``funcnames``/``constants`` print the tree-sitter views, and ``--scope``, ``--kinds``, ``--layout`` and ``--archives`` control what is included (zip, wheel, tar and zstd archives are scanned too).

xrar.py.summary: Extract the RAR archives below a directory, including their split parts.
details: Finds the ``.rar`` files, resolves the ``.partN.rar``/``.rNN`` companions, extracts each of them in a process pool into a folder next to the archive and reports the resulting size.
Unpacks each zip file into a temporary directory, creates a ``.tar.xz`` with tar and replaces the original archive with the compressed result.

zshdiag.py.summary: Diagnose a zsh setup: duplicate aliases, functions and shadowed binaries.
details: Collects the aliases and functions defined in ``~/.zshrc``, ``~/.config/zsh.d`` and ``~/.oh-my-zsh``, lists the definitions that appear more than once with their source files and shows which commands are shadowed by other binaries on ``PATH``.
